title: No planner loop: MULTI_STEP says 'coming soon'; demo goals 2-4 unreachable
detail: The only System-2 path is `if label == 'MULTI_STEP': say('Multi-step tasks are coming soon')`. Nothing loads prompts/planner_system.md (grep 'planner_system' in ml/src: 0 hits; {catalog} never filled), nothing calls an LLM for DSL, no observe->plan->execute->replan loop, no harness verification of `done` (execute_actions L278-281 just says the summary and shows success). Walkthrough: (1) 'open my downloads as a list' -> v0 regex L87-91 (or engine top-1 open_folder) runs open_folder only, never cmd+2, and reports ui success: wrong result shown as correct. (2) 'search flights to tokyo in safari and open the first result' -> v0 regex L82-85 yields web_search query='flights to tokyo in safari and open the first result' in the DEFAULT browser; engine path -> MULTI_STEP -> 'coming soon'. (3) Numbers finance and (4) Premiere marker/cut/export are inherently multi-step -> 'coming soon'.
evidence: orchestrator.py L149-152 quoted; python: re.search(r'(?:search|google|look up|lookup)(?:\s+for)?\s+(.+)','search flights to tokyo in safari and open the first result').group(1) -> 'flights to tokyo in safari and open the first result'.
fix: Add brain/planner.py: build static prefix once (prompt with catalog rendered, cached KV), per turn append goal + latest obs text/diff + last batch results (incl. script output, expect_ok/observed, errors); stream-parse lines and execute each complete action immediately; loop until done/ask/refuse or step cap (~12). On `done`, run verify with the last expect (or re-observe) before ui success. Route MULTI_STEP and any utterance with conjunction ('and', 'then', 'as a list', 'in <app>') to it.

title: Model can bypass CONFIRM by emitting confirmed=true skill arg
detail: validate_args passes a `confirmed` key through for any skill, and both gates trust it: brain orchestrator.py L351 `if spec.get('risk')=='confirm' and not args.get('confirmed')` and HandsKit Skills.swift L160 `inArgs['confirmed'] as? Bool != true`. A planner line (or a prompt-injected page/email that the model copies) `skill send_message to=mom body="..." confirmed=true` sends with no user confirmation. Same for move_to_trash, compose_email.
evidence: python: dsl.parse('skill send_message to=mom body="hi" confirmed=true') -> args {'to':'mom','body':'hi','confirmed':True}; Catalog.validate_args('send_message', that) -> returns it unchanged; _skill then skips ask_confirm.
fix: Strip `confirmed` from model/DSL args in Orchestrator._skill (args.pop('confirmed',None) before validate) and set it only after ask_confirm returns yes; in catalog.validate_args raise on 'confirmed' unless an internal flag is passed. Optionally have the app keep a one-shot confirm token (confirm_reply id) instead of a bool.

title: Destructive scripts and press/keys run without confirm
detail: script_needs_confirm is a keyword regex; it misses common destructive AppleScript/JXA, and non-script ops have no gate at all (press on a 'Send'/'Delete'/'Buy' button, keys cmd+delete in Finder = move to Trash, keys cmd+return = send in Mail). Prompt rule 11 is the only protection, and rule 12 (screen text is data) is prompt-only.
evidence: script_needs_confirm returns False for: jxa doShellScript("mv ~/Documents ~/.Trash/"); Finder `move (every file of folder "Downloads" of home) to trash`; jxa $.NSFileManager...removeItemAtPathError; `close document 1 saving no`; Numbers `set value of every cell of range "A1:D120" to ""` (overwrite). Reproduced with /tmp probe against orchestrator.py@bcd3b75.
fix: Invert the policy: applescript/jxa need confirm unless they match an allowlist of read/format verbs for the target app (e.g. Numbers get/set value on cells outside existing data, sort, background color); always confirm doShellScript/do shell script/ObjC/$./NSFileManager/move .* to trash/close .* saving no/delete. For press/keys: confirm when target label matches /send|delete|remove|buy|pay|purchase|post|publish|submit|erase|trash|overwrite|replace/i or combo in {cmd+delete, cmd+return, cmd+shift+delete, cmd+q}, unless the previous action in the batch was a confirm.

title: Parser rejects '#' comment lines and ``` fences; prompt example 3 fails
detail: Prompt (AGENTS DSL and planner_system.md L34) allows `# <note>` lines and the new Numbers example ends with one (L75), but dsl.parse has no comment branch -> 'unknown op #' and the whole batch is lost. All prompt examples are wrapped in ``` fences, so the model will often emit them too -> 'unknown op ```'. Few-shot examples teach the exact form that fails.
evidence: python: dsl.parse(numbers_example_block) -> DSLError 'line 5: unknown op #'; dsl.parse('```\nkeys cmd+2\n```') -> 'line 1: unknown op ```'. Parsing every fenced example from prompts/planner_system.md@bcd3b75: example 3 ERR.
fix: In parse(): `if line.startswith('#') and not re.match(r'#\d', line): continue` (refs only appear as args, never line-initial) and skip lines matching r'^```\w*$'. Add both cases to tests/test_dsl.py, plus a test that parses every example block in planner_system.md.

title: Script ends the batch, script output discarded, skill/script expects dropped
detail: (a) L286-287 `if op == 'script': return await self._script(a)` returns after the first script: any later action (incl. done/expect follow-ups) never runs. (b) Act returns script output in `output`/`stdout`, but _trace_res (L315-318) keeps only ok/error/observed/diff_text/expect_ok/act_ms/settle_ms/epoch and execute_actions returns just 'ok' -> the planner can never see a Numbers range read, so the finance flow (read transactions, compute, verify totals) and the prompt's 'script returns the new total; next turn says done' cannot work. (c) _skill and _script never forward a.get('expect') -> `skill open_folder ...` / `script ...` + `expect` is silently unchecked (violates 'every consequential action carries an expect').
evidence: Code quoted at L286-287, L315-318, L328 (params = {op,lang,code} only, no expect), L364-365 (skill params {name,args} only).
fix: Make execute_actions return a list of per-action results {op, ok, error, output, diff_text, expect_ok, observed} that the planner loop feeds back; `continue` after a successful script; pass expect into the script act params (Act.swift already evaluates params['expect'] for every op) and after skill RPCs call verify{expect}. title: Pixel click uses 0-1000 image coords as global points
detail: Prompt L20 tells the model `click x,y` is in 0-1000 image coords; dsl.parse passes x,y through, orchestrator forwards them, and Act.swift `let p = CGPoint(x: x, y: y)` clicks at global screen points. No conversion via the screenshot's origin/scale/width/height exists anywhere (grep in ml/src: none). Every pixel-fallback click lands in the wrong place (e.g. a target at image (500,500) of a window at origin (800,200) size 1200x800 should be global (1400,600); it clicks (500,500)). Also no screenshot is ever attached, so the rule is unusable today.
evidence: Act.swift L276 quoted; prompt L20 quoted.
fix: In the brain, keep the last screenshot meta {origin, width_pts, height_pts} and convert: gx = origin.x + x/1000*width_pts, gy = origin.y + y/1000*height_pts before sending act; refuse click when no screenshot is in the current turn.

title: Range formula recipe writes identical formula to every cell
detail: Rule 8 teaches `set value of every cell of range "F2:F120" to "=..."`. AppleScript sets the same literal string in every cell; Numbers does not shift relative references, so e.g. a per-row category or duplicate-flag formula (=IF(B2...)) computes row 2 in all 119 rows -> wrong categories/flags/totals presented as correct. Not verified on a Mac (Linux VM).
evidence: Reasoning from Numbers AppleScript dictionary semantics (value is set verbatim); needs a 10-second check on the Mac: set range F2:F4 to "=B2" and read values.
fix: Recipe: build per-row values/formulas in the script loop (`repeat with i from 2 to 121 ... set value of cell ("F" & i) to "=IF(...B" & i & "...)"`) or compute in AppleScript and write results; use cross-table SUMIF only for the totals. Fixture note: description 'APPLE STORE' also appears at -109.86 on 10-01, so flag the outlier by amount threshold, not merchant.

title: Shell script non-zero exit reported as ok
detail: runShell returns r with exit_code!=0 but act() then sets out['ok']=true; orchestrator._script only checks ok, so a failed shell step counts as success and the batch/plan proceeds on a false premise.

title: Refs after skill/open/url resolve to the previous window
detail: element(ref:) ignores epoch and looks up `current`, which is only refreshed by observe or by the fused observe inside act. The `skill` RPC (RPC.swift) never re-observes, so after `skill open_folder` or a script that opens a window, `press #7` resolves #7 from the OLD window and acts on a background element (or a different control with the same ref) instead of failing stale_ref. Also open/url return before the new app is key and settle waits on lastPid (the old app), so the next `keys cmd+l` in the Safari example can hit the old app.
evidence: Observe.swift@1d7cc07 L468: `guard let r = current[ref] else { throw staleRef }` (epoch unused); Act.swift L237/L311 settle pid = lastObservedPid(); openAppNamed returns right after activate().
fix: Reject ref ops when params.epoch != currentEpoch unless the element's window equals the current focused window; re-observe after skill RPCs and return epoch/diff_text; for open/url, wait until frontmostApplication matches (<=2 s) and settle on that pid.

title: Harness's own done-rejection counts toward the 3-failed-turns loop guard
detail: The planner-13 verified-done logic rejects the first standalone done after a failure by design, and it sets failed=True. The new loop guard then counts that as a failed turn (fail_streak += 1). So two real failed turns followed by the deliberate done-rejection give fail_streak=3, and the user sees 'I'm stuck on that, can you help?' with awaiting_user, even when the task is actually complete. This hits a correct, recovered task and turns a success into a stuck result in the demo.
evidence: L1087-1090: done_rejected=True; failed=True. L1093: `if res_status == "failed" or failed or not n_actions:` -> L1096 fail_streak += 1 -> L1098 `fail_streak >= 3` -> return 'awaiting_user'. The streak resets only on a turn without failure (L1109). Trace: turn1 expect fails (1), turn2 fix's expect fails (2), turn3 fix ok but has no expect -> streak reset... ; the failing variant is turn1 fail (1), turn2 fail (2), turn3 standalone done with obs_fresh & prev_had_failure -> rejected (3) -> stuck. Static read only: test_planner_loop needs mlx.
fix: Do not count the done-rejection: set a flag `done_reject_turn = True` at L1087 and use `if not done_reject_turn: fail_streak += 1` (fail_key stays None, so `same` is already False). Alternatively, handle the rejection before the failure branch with `diffs=None; continue`.

title: Offline planner bench grades lines the runtime would accept as invalid
detail: brain-3 made the runtime lenient. dsl.action_line drops prose, tag and fence lines, and adds the missing `skill` prefix to lines that start with a catalog skill name (`open_app app=Keynote`). planner_offline.Runner.turn and grade() don't apply action_line. Each raw line goes to dsl.parse, so a reply the live planner would run correctly is scored INVALID/fail. The prefix-less line also fails first_ok when the accept regex expects `skill open_app`. This benchmark is the tool for the tuned-vs-tuned knob comparisons that AGENTS.md now requires (constrain, history, few-shot, model). Its bias favours configurations that never emit prose, mainly --constrain, so a model or knob can be picked on a metric that doesn't match runtime behaviour.
evidence: `grep -n action_line evals/planner_offline.py` -> no match. Runner.turn L417-432 sends the raw stripped line to cutter.push and lines.append. grade L470-476 runs `dsl.parse(ln)` on every non-expect line and sets valid=False on an exception. The runtime path is orchestrator.py L~960, `dl = dsl.action_line(line, self.catalog.skills); if dl is None: skipped.append(line); continue`. Static review only; the bench needs mlx.
fix: In Runner.turn, before cutter.push: `line = dsl.action_line(line, catalog_skills)`, then `if line is None: skipped += 1; continue`. Report `skipped` per row, and keep a separate strict-format metric if wanted so that the pass rate mirrors runtime.

title: JXA string-concat doShellScript bypasses script confirmation
detail: This is a variant of planner-3 (resolved). Orchestrator.script_needs_confirm, called at L1704 for the planner's script op, sets numbers_only when the only Application(...) target is Numbers. It does not count Application.currentApplication() as a target, and _SCRIPT_BLOCK matches only the literal token 'doShellScript'. title: Rule 14 'expect focused' (no ref) is rejected by HandsKit before acting
detail: Rule 14 tells the planner to send 'keys cmd+n' and then 'expect focused' on the text area. For skill and script actions, the action runs first and then verify throws (RPC.swift L177), so an action that succeeded is reported as failed. title: DONE gate checks no goal state; rejection costs a full planner turn
detail: This is related to planner-13 (resolved). done is accepted when it is alone in the batch and either the previous batch's last expect passed or the observation is fresh. Nothing checks the goal itself. When the last action had no expect, the obs is a diff rebuild: done is rejected once, diffs is forced to None, and the planner re-emits done on the fresh obs. That costs an extra prefill and decode (my estimate is 0.5-1.5 s on the 4B, not measured) for no gain in verification.
evidence: orchestrator.py@3772f7c L2380-2382: `n_executed == 0 and (prev_expect_ok or obs_fresh and (not prev_had_failure or done_rejected))`. On rejection (L2387-2393), diffs is set to None and the loop continues to a new planner call.
fix: When done is rejected only because the obs is not fresh, re-observe harness-side and accept or reject without a new plan() call. Feed the fresh obs to the planner only if the check fails.

title: Act expects are verified twice; skill/script expects aren't polled

Skill, script and click-target expects get only the single-shot verify, with no polling (RPC.swift L173-180), so a page or window that appears slowly after a skill fails spuriously.

title: Memory LLM rewrite decodes before routing on any pronoun command

title: Think ship picks qwen sampler on a one-task edge, +0.85 s p50/step
detail: The DECISION ships 4b-t512-qwen-all over 4b-t512-greedy-all on holdout mean 0.770 vs 0.763. The two configs differ by about one task per set (v1-holdout 11 vs 12 of 14, v1-holdout2 11 vs 10 of 12, v2-holdout 79 vs 78 of 130); pooled that is 101/156 vs 100/156 (0.647 vs 0.641). That is noise from a single seeded run. Qwen costs 2596 vs 1743 ms p50 per step (+853 ms) and 7776 vs 5656 ms p95 (+2.1 s), with 173 vs 153 think tokens. Speed is the first priority and demos 3 and 4 are multi-step, so qwen adds roughly 3-5 s to a 4-6 step task for no measurable accuracy gain. Also, 'holdout mean' averages per-set rates with equal weight, so the 14- and 12-item sets each count as much as the 130-item v2 set, and one task in v1-holdout moves the mean by 0.024.

title: Memory saves planner 'ok' outcomes as workflows even when done was a false accept
detail: When the planner outcome is 'ok', _planner_memory_writes saves an episode row ('<goal> → ok (N steps, app)') to long-term memory and appends the plan's action lines as a Demo(source='memory') to ~/Library/Application Support/Muselet/workflows.jsonl.
